text:
COLUMBUS, Ohio — An Oberlin College professor and his wife are dead, and the educator's 31-year-old child is being held on a $3 million bond and facing murder charges in their deaths.

The bodies of Pipo Nguyen-Duy, 64, a studio art and photography professor and acclaimed fine art photographer, and his wife, Tran Thi Nam Phong, 56, were found shot in their home a few blocks off campus on Wednesday, according to police. The professor was on the first floor of the home, his wife on the second.

Asia Nguyen-Duy, previously known as Daniel Jones, of Ashland, Oregon, was arraigned Thursday on charges of murder, felonious assault and tampering with evidence, according to court filings. A motive has not yet been released.

The younger Nguyen-Duy, face tattooed and bloodied, was initially carried into the municipal courtroom before later being wheeled in a chair. The suspect said they are gender neutral and no longer go by the name Daniel Jones. Identification found in a car that police found set afire near the college's conservatory of music, which led them to the scene of the crime, listed the name Daniel Jones.

Oberlin City Prosecutor Zachary Simonoff told the judge that the accused had offered a confession to the crimes and led them to the father and stepmother's address.

Simonoff also told Oberlin Municipal Court Judge Farah Emeka that the defendant's mother had been in touch with police to let them know that her child was “currently psychotic” and needed medication. A message was left with Asia's attorney.

The case has been bound over to Lorain County Common Pleas Court, where it will next go before a grand jury. The suspect is being held in the Lorain County Jail.

The deaths have rocked the private liberal arts college, where students had just returned this week from fall break.

Studio art classes were paused or modified in the wake of the professor's death. An exhibit of his internationally acclaimed photography was placed on display at the campus art museum to provide students, alumni and collaborators a place to gather and reflect. A memorial tribute for Nguyen-Duy, who arrived at Oberlin in 1998, also is being planned.

Digital forums for sharing condolences and memories also were set up by Oberlin and some regional institutions, including the Museum of Contemporary Art Cleveland.

Carmen Twillie Ambar, president of Oberlin College and Conservatory, called it “a deeply challenging moment for our community.”

“Tragedies such as this one intrude upon our lives in jarring ways,” she wrote in an open letter. “I am simply overwhelmed with sadness, and I am deeply concerned about the impact of the devastating loss of Pipo to our community.”

Pipo Nguyen-Duy was also mourned by the Guggenheim Foundation, where he was a 2011 photography fellow. The foundation said he immigrated to the U.S. from Vietnam in 1975 and took up photography in his late 20s. He had a bachelor's degree in economics from Carleton College and both a master of arts and a master of fine arts degrees from the University of New Mexico at Albuquerque.

“In his wide-ranging body of work, Nguyen-duy considered immigration and emigration, intimacy, abandonment and decay, cultural assimilation, and the cost of war,” the foundation said on Instagram.

text:
$AMZN KEY READ-THROUGHS FROM AMAZON’S Q3 2026 EARNINGS CALL

Amazon’s results reinforce a consequential divergence across the AI economy: infrastructure demand is accelerating, but the distribution of economic returns is becoming less favorable to undifferentiated capacity providers and more favorable to scarce-component suppliers, efficient computing architectures, and established platforms. AWS grew 39.3%, backlog reached $578 billion, and management projected growth above 40% in both 2027 and 2028. However, Amazon’s trailing free-cash-flow outflow of $42.4 billion demonstrates that strong demand does not automatically translate into attractive near-term shareholder cash returns. Outside technology infrastructure, improving delivery economics, grocery adoption, and integrated advertising tools strengthen Amazon’s competitive position against less diversified incumbents. The highest-conviction implications are therefore selective rather than uniformly bullish or bearish for technology, consumer spending, or digital advertising. Country labels below refer to corporate domicile; magnitude assessments describe business exposure, not predicted share-price returns.

SEMICONDUCTORS AND MEMORY

MEMORY SUPPLIERS RETAIN PRICING POWER EVEN AS HYPERSCALERS INTERNALIZE ACCELERATOR DESIGN (READ-THROUGH 1)

Affected companies: Micron Technology (MU: United States) and SK hynix (000660: South Korea). Direction: Positive. Magnitude: High for data-center memory demand and earnings durability; moderate incremental information beyond their already-reported results.

Amazon’s commentary provides unusually useful customer-side confirmation of memory suppliers’ pricing position. Management acknowledged “heightened component costs like memory,” maintained approximately $220 billion of 2026 cash capital expenditures, and expects meaningfully higher spending in 2027. AWS’s core compute and storage businesses also grew at their fastest rates in several years. The implication extends beyond accelerator-attached high-bandwidth memory to server DRAM and enterprise storage supporting production inference, data retrieval, and CPU-intensive agent workflows.

The transmission mechanism is stronger memory consumption combined with customer willingness to continue deploying infrastructure despite elevated component costs. Amazon can reduce dependence on merchant accelerator margins through Trainium, but proprietary accelerator design does not eliminate the requirement for advanced memory. Consequently, the shift toward custom silicon does not have the same adverse competitive implications for memory manufacturers that it has for merchant accelerator suppliers. Amazon’s commitment to further investment also reduces the immediate risk that memory inflation alone forces a broad infrastructure spending retrenchment.

The timing distinction matters. SK hynix’s October 28 results had already disclosed long-term agreements covering more than 50% of 2027-2028 production capacity, with pricing mechanisms operating within agreed ranges. Micron had already reported strong results on September 30. Amazon therefore corroborates the durability of the cycle rather than revealing an undiscovered current-quarter earnings catalyst. The more important fundamental effect concerns 2027 contract negotiations, product mix, and capacity utilization. Supplier allocations and memory content per Amazon system remain undisclosed, so no specific AWS procurement share or proportional earnings uplift can be assigned to either company.

AGENTIC COMPUTING STRENGTHENS ARM’S ROYALTY OPPORTUNITY, NOT JUST ACCELERATOR DEMAND (READ-THROUGH 2)

Affected company: Arm Holdings (ARM: United Kingdom). Direction: Positive. Magnitude: High for the data-center franchise; moderate for consolidated earnings because AWS-specific royalty economics are undisclosed.

Jassy highlighted CPU demand associated with reinforcement-learning workflows, post-training support, and agent tool use. He also stated that Graviton offers up to 30%-40% better price-performance than alternatives, that Graviton revenue commitments increased more than 20x year-over-year, and that backlog for older Graviton generations more than doubled sequentially after Graviton5 launched. These disclosures indicate that AI growth is expanding demand for general-purpose processing rather than simply replacing CPU workloads with accelerators.

The connection to Arm is direct: Graviton uses Arm technology, and Arm has publicly described Graviton and Nitro performing host-processing and networking functions alongside Trainium. Increased deployment therefore supports Arm’s licensing and production-royalty opportunity across both conventional cloud workloads and AI infrastructure. The continued demand for older Graviton generations is particularly relevant because it suggests broader workload adoption rather than demand concentrated exclusively in the newest processor launch.

The principal catalyst is conversion of AWS capacity commitments into deployed silicon during 2027-2028. Arm’s latest reported quarter already showed data-center royalties more than doubling, so Amazon confirms an established adoption trend rather than predicting an unreported historical result. Crucially, AWS’s more than 20x increase in revenue commitments does not imply 20x processor shipments or Arm royalties. It also does not represent an order for Arm’s separately marketed AGI CPU. The high-conviction conclusion is stronger architecture adoption and royalty durability, not a quantifiable AWS-driven earnings revision.

CUSTOM ACCELERATORS CHANGE THE CHIP DESIGN WINNER MORE THAN THE FOUNDRY BENEFICIARY (READ-THROUGH 3)

Affected company: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (2330/TSM: Taiwan). Direction: Positive. Magnitude: High for leading-edge manufacturing demand durability; moderate incremental benefit from this specific call.

Jassy described advanced-chip production as concentrated at a common manufacturing provider, with customers receiving allocations and deciding how to deploy that constrained supply. Amazon also reported installing an AI accelerator approximately every 14 seconds and emphasized substantial capacity additions over the next 8-10 quarters. Public hardware reporting identifies TSMC as the manufacturer behind Amazon’s advanced custom processors, while TSMC’s own October 15 results confirmed strong leading-edge demand.

The economic implication is that Trainium’s success need not be negative for the manufacturing layer even when it challenges merchant accelerator economics. More custom designs can redirect semiconductor spending among chip vendors while preserving demand for advanced wafers and packaging. TSMC is therefore exposed to the expansion of AI compute across competing architectures, rather than requiring a particular merchant GPU supplier to retain its existing share.

The most important qualification concerns external Trainium sales beginning in late 2027. Amazon explicitly said those sales compete with internal cloud deployment for allocated chips. Selling the same chip externally rather than installing it in AWS does not create an additional foundry order. Incremental manufacturing demand requires a larger production allocation or higher total chip output. Near-term, Amazon corroborates TSMC’s already-reported demand strength; the longer-duration catalyst is expansion of qualified manufacturing and packaging capacity through 2027-2028. Taiwanese geographic concentration remains a shared risk across otherwise competing AI investments.

TRAINIUM WEAKENS NVIDIA’S INFERENCE PRICING POSITION WITHOUT SIGNALING AN IMMEDIATE DEMAND CONTRACTION (READ-THROUGH 4)

Affected company: NVIDIA (NVDA: United States). Direction: Negative for long-duration inference share and pricing power; not evidence of a near-term revenue decline. Magnitude: Potentially high within hyperscaler inference, but unquantifiable at the consolidated level.

The strongest evidence is already operational rather than purely prospective. Jassy confirmed that “the majority and most of Bedrock today is being run on top of Trainium.” Inference accounts for well over half of AWS AI revenue, while Amazon is reducing software-porting friction through TorchNeuron and intends to offer Trainium outside AWS in late 2027. Together, these disclosures show that a major cloud platform is using proprietary accelerators for a commercially important inference service and is preparing to extend that alternative beyond its own infrastructure.

The transmission mechanism is reduced merchant accelerator content per unit of inference growth and stronger customer negotiating leverage. A hyperscaler with credible internal hardware can choose between buying merchant systems, deploying its own chips, or offering customers lower-priced managed inference. Wider PyTorch compatibility reduces an adoption obstacle, although compatibility alone does not establish equivalent performance across every workload. External Trainium availability could further broaden the competitive set for customers that previously lacked access outside AWS.

The negative implication concerns future economic rents, not an imminent collapse in NVIDIA demand. NVIDIA’s latest reported quarter showed data-center revenue increasing 117%, and Amazon’s infrastructure expansion enlarges the overall compute market. NVIDIA also retains advantages in software, networking, system integration, and workload breadth. The relevant 2027-2028 catalysts are verified production adoption, external Trainium shipment scale, and changes in realized pricing or customer mix. Treating Amazon’s entire capital budget as NVIDIA-addressable spending is increasingly inappropriate; treating Trainium’s success as proof of near-term NVIDIA revenue weakness is equally unsupported.

DATA-CENTER EQUIPMENT AND ELECTRICITY

POWER AND THERMAL EQUIPMENT BENEFIT FROM THE BUILDOUT BEFORE CLOUD OWNERS EARN THEIR FULL RETURNS (READ-THROUGH 5)

Affected company: Vertiv Holdings (VRT: United States). Direction: Positive. Magnitude: High for medium-term demand visibility; limited incremental surprise for the already-reported Q3.

Amazon maintained approximately $220 billion of 2026 capital spending, expects meaningfully higher spending in 2027, and described large capacity reservations extending through 2028 and into 2029. Jassy emphasized that customers reserve blocks of hundreds of megawatts and sometimes approximately 1 gigawatt. Those are physical infrastructure commitments requiring electrical distribution, power conditioning, thermal management, and supporting services, irrespective of whether the compute hardware uses merchant GPUs or proprietary accelerators.

Vertiv’s transmission mechanism is equipment and service demand associated with constructing and operating that capacity. Its opportunity is less dependent on which accelerator architecture wins than on the amount and density of infrastructure commissioned. Importantly, equipment revenue can be recognized during construction and deployment, well before Amazon reaches the full payback on the completed data center. Amazon’s weak near-term free cash flow can therefore coexist with strong supplier earnings and cash generation.

Vertiv had already reported more than 100% organic order growth on October 28. Amazon’s call is corroboration of that demand environment, not a prediction of Vertiv’s completed quarter. The incremental fundamental support concerns 2027-2028 order conversion and sustained investment beyond the current construction wave. No Amazon-specific award or supplier allocation was disclosed, so the call does not justify assigning a defined portion of the capital budget to Vertiv. Power availability, construction delays, and customer acceptance can still defer equipment conversion without implying demand cancellation.

CONTRACTED NUCLEAR POWER HAS A MORE DIRECT CASH-FLOW CHANNEL THAN GENERIC AI ELECTRICITY EXPOSURE (READ-THROUGH 6)

Affected company: Talen Energy (TLN: United States). Direction: Positive. Magnitude: Moderate incremental support for contract durability; high strategic relevance to the contracted nuclear asset.

Amazon’s comments about advance reservations for very large power blocks and its expectation of more than 40% AWS growth in both 2027 and 2028 reinforce the need for dependable electricity supply. The company-specific connection is established: Talen’s disclosed agreement provides for up to 1,920 megawatts of Susquehanna nuclear power to Amazon through 2042, with deliveries ramping over time and full volume expected no later than 2032.

The mechanism is delivery under an existing long-duration commercial arrangement, not an assumed increase in merchant electricity prices. Amazon’s infrastructure demand supports the economic rationale for the contracted load and the durability of the customer relationship. This is a more concrete exposure than simply owning a generator located somewhere near prospective data-center development.

However, the call did not announce a larger Talen contract, a higher contract price, or an accelerated Pennsylvania delivery schedule. Amazon’s global capacity requirements cannot be allocated automatically to Susquehanna. Talen had already raised its own outlook in August, so this is supporting evidence for an existing investment framework rather than a new quantified earnings upgrade. The relevant catalysts are verified delivery milestones, interconnection readiness, and disclosed contract amendments during 2027 onward. Grid constraints, regulatory conditions, and nuclear operating performance remain more important to near-term realization than headline AI token growth.

CLOUD INFRASTRUCTURE AND ENTERPRISE SOFTWARE

DATADOG’S CONSUMPTION OPPORTUNITY IMPROVES EVEN AS AMAZON’S EQUITY REACTS NEGATIVELY (READ-THROUGH 7)

Affected company: Datadog (DDOG: United States). Direction: Positive. Magnitude: Moderate fundamental tailwind; no defensible proportional earnings uplift from AWS growth alone.

Amazon reported that core compute and storage revenue grew at their fastest rates in several years, Bedrock token volume increased nearly 17x, and customers deployed more agents during Q3 than in the preceding 3 quarters combined. These are favorable indicators for the volume and complexity of production workloads requiring monitoring. They are more relevant to Datadog’s demand than Amazon’s capital-spending burden or below-consensus consolidated operating-income outlook.

The relationship is operationally verified. AWS and Datadog have documented an integration that monitors Bedrock agent executions, model calls, tool invocations, and knowledge-base interactions. More production applications and more complex agent workflows can increase demand for infrastructure monitoring, application performance management, logs, tracing, and LLM observability. Lower inference costs can also expand the set of economically viable applications, increasing monitoring requirements even as revenue per token falls.

This is a particularly important distinction given the supplied notice’s report that Datadog shares followed Amazon lower. The call does not establish a deterioration in Datadog’s addressable workload demand. Datadog’s already-reported Q2 growth of 36% and positive free cash flow provide separate evidence that its economics should not be conflated with a hyperscaler’s construction cycle.

The near-term catalyst is Datadog’s next usage and customer-expansion disclosure; the longer-duration driver is production adoption during 2027-2028. The limitations are meaningful: customers can sample telemetry, optimize retention, or use AWS-native tools, and additional tokens do not translate mechanically into additional billable monitoring units. The positive read-through is a stronger consumption environment, not proof of a specific revenue beat.

VERTICAL INTEGRATION RAISES THE RETURN HURDLE FOR MERCHANT GPU CLOUDS (READ-THROUGH 8)

Affected company: CoreWeave (CRWV: United States). Direction: Negative for long-term competitive economics and the margin of safety required in valuation. Magnitude: High strategic relevance; limited evidence of immediate contracted-revenue impairment.

Jassy distinguished AWS from businesses primarily hosting GPUs or renting short-duration capacity, describing AWS as “a long-term platform strategy.” He emphasized owned or long-leased infrastructure, custom chips, and the ability to place inference close to customers’ existing applications and data. These advantages matter most when supply scarcity becomes less dominant and customers can compare full delivered cost, reliability, and platform functionality.

The transmission mechanism is pressure on future contract pricing and renewal economics. AWS can combine lower hardware acquisition costs, shared infrastructure, and multiple monetization layers, while using cheaper inference to attract additional compute, storage, and software consumption. A merchant GPU cloud must earn an adequate return on purchased hardware and financing without necessarily capturing the same broader platform revenue. Amazon’s willingness to continue investing despite negative near-term free cash flow also signals sustained competitive capacity expansion rather than a disciplined industry-wide supply response.

CoreWeave’s own disclosures demonstrate why demand and shareholder returns must be separated. It reported approximately $104 billion of June-end backlog and more than $25 billion of additional commitments early in Q3, but Q2 net interest expense was $640 million. Operating cash flow was positive $679 million, an important counterweight to a simplistic liquidity-collapse narrative. Strong bookings and improving operating cash flow do not remove sensitivity to financing costs, equipment replacement, and future utilization.

Amazon’s asserted margin advantage should not be transferred directly into a quantified CoreWeave disadvantage because the companies have different business mixes, asset structures, and accounting profiles. Existing contracts also cannot be assumed to reprice immediately. The next financing and deployment disclosures are the near-term catalysts; the more significant fundamental test arrives with renewals, new contract cohorts, and hardware replacement during 2027-2029. The bearish conclusion concerns the durability of excess returns, not the existence of current AI demand.

DIGITAL ADVERTISING

AMAZON’S FULL-FUNNEL AUTOMATION THREATENS INDEPENDENT AD-TECH ECONOMICS MORE THAN ITS QUARTERLY AD MISS SUGGESTS (READ-THROUGH 9)

Affected company: The Trade Desk (TTD: United States). Direction: Negative. Magnitude: Moderate-to-high competitive significance; the current call does not quantify displaced spending.

Amazon’s approximately 12% constant-currency advertising growth should not be read as a straightforward easing of competitive pressure. Management attributed much of the slowdown to Prime Day timing, sports scheduling, and comparison effects, and expects growth to return to the high teens in Q4. More importantly, Amazon introduced an AI-first advertising platform and full-funnel campaigns combining sponsored ads, display, video, and streaming television. Advertisers provide inputs such as budget and duration, while Amazon’s systems plan, execute, and optimize the campaign.

The competitive mechanism is the combination of advertising workflow automation with proprietary commerce signals and transaction measurement. Amazon can connect product discovery, audience selection, advertising exposure, and purchase outcomes within an integrated offering. That reduces the operational burden of managing separate campaign components and can encourage advertisers to consolidate incremental budgets on Amazon’s platform.

For The Trade Desk, the risk is not simply losing a bidding algorithm comparison. It is losing influence over campaign orchestration and budget allocation to a platform that also owns inventory, customer relationships, and purchase data. The Trade Desk’s independence and cross-publisher reach remain differentiators, but those advantages must offset the convenience and measurement benefits of Amazon’s integrated system.

The Trade Desk’s already-reported Q2 revenue growth of 3% establishes that its growth challenge predates this call; Amazon’s announcement should not be retroactively assigned as the cause. Customer retention above 95% is also compatible with slower spending growth or wallet-share pressure. The near-term catalyst is Q4 advertising budget allocation and Amazon’s expected growth rebound. The longer-duration issue is 2027 platform adoption and whether campaign automation pressures independent-platform spending growth or monetization. The high-conviction negative is intensified competition, not a claim that specific advertiser contracts have already migrated.

FOOD RETAIL AND CONSUMER DISTRIBUTION

AMAZON’S GROCERY COST ADVANTAGE IS MORE THREATENING THAN ITS GROCERY SALES HEADLINE (READ-THROUGH 10)

Affected companies: Albertsons Companies (ACI: United States) and The Kroger Co. (KR: United States). Direction: Negative competitive pressure, stronger for Albertsons. Magnitude: Moderate-to-high earnings sensitivity for Albertsons; moderate strategic pressure for Kroger.

Amazon reported that fresh groceries and everyday essentials grew approximately 3x faster than the rest of its store and represented approximately half of units sold. More consequentially, it expects a 4th consecutive annual reduction in cost to serve. Shipping costs excluding fuel and linehaul inflation grew approximately 8%, versus approximately 12% unit growth. The emerging competitive advantage is therefore not merely faster digital sales growth. It is the ability to expand grocery delivery while improving the underlying delivery-cost structure.

The transmission mechanism has 2 parts. First, perishables can capture frequent shopping missions and redirect spending on adjacent household categories. Second, incumbent grocers may need to respond with sharper pricing, delivery subsidies, loyalty spending, and fulfillment investment. Lost volume creates fixed-cost deleverage, while defensive spending can pressure margins even if market share is retained.

Albertsons’ October results illustrate the vulnerability. Digital sales increased 11%, but the company attributed gross-margin pressure partly to higher delivery and handling costs. Identical sales declined 0.8%, and adjusted EBITDA margin was approximately 4.1%. Amazon is therefore expanding a service whose economics are improving while Albertsons is absorbing additional costs to grow its own digital channel. Illustratively, an additional 25-basis-point margin burden at unchanged sales would equal approximately 6% of Albertsons’ reported quarterly adjusted EBITDA. That is a sensitivity, not a forecast of an Amazon-induced earnings decline.

Kroger has stronger counterevidence. Its digital business was profitable on the company’s disclosed basis, which includes third-party media revenue, and adjusted e-commerce growth reached 20% after specified business exits. The negative read-through is therefore less severe and should not be treated as identical across the 2 grocers. Amazon’s international and broad everyday-essential metrics also cannot be converted directly into U.S. supermarket market-share losses.

Near-term catalysts are holiday pricing, delivery economics, and subsequent identical-sales disclosures. The longer-duration shift concerns household shopping frequency and the cost of maintaining digital relevance over 2027-2028. Amazon’s 7x everyday-essential purchase comparison for perishables customers is observational, not proof that grocery adoption causes the entire spending difference. The strongest conclusion is sustained competitive pressure on cost structure and customer retention, particularly where incumbent digital growth is already margin-dilutive.

text:
Outlier of the Day (October 30, 2026): Mo Ibrahim, The Engineer Who Wired Africa Without Paying a Single Bribe

Field: Telecommunications / Entrepreneurship / Philanthropy

In the late 1990s, a Sudanese engineer went looking for money to build mobile networks in Africa. Bank after bank turned him down. Part of the problem was a perception that African countries were corrupt. One contact, offered a free telecom license in Uganda, asked him in disbelief whether he really expected his board to invest there. Mo Ibrahim built it anyway, and it made him a billionaire.

Born on 3 May 1946 in Sudan, of Nubian descent, he was the second of five children. His family moved to Egypt, where his father worked for a cotton company and his mother was determined that all the children be educated. As a boy, his bedroom walls carried posters of Einstein and Marie Curie.

Academic journey: He graduated in electrical engineering from Alexandria University in 1968, worked for Sudan's state telecom company in Khartoum, then left for the UK to study mobile communications, earning a master's at Bradford and a PhD at Birmingham. His research was in the then-unfashionable field of mobile communications, specifically reusing radio frequencies.

Work history: In 1983 he became technical director at Cellnet (now O2), where he launched the first cellular network in the UK. His turning point was frustration. He found BT a huge bureaucracy that failed to see the future, so he decided to do what he knew: grow networks. He founded consultancy MSI in 1989, selling it for around $900 million in 2000, and launched Celtel in 1998.

The edge: Integrity as strategy. To make the no-bribe vow real, nobody in the company could spend more than $30,000 without the signatures of the entire board. When disputes arose, he sued three African governments in local courts and won every case. When he sold Celtel in 2005 for $3.4 billion, it had over 24 million subscribers in 14 African countries.

Perspective: He calls himself an "accidental businessman." Rather than retire, he launched a foundation and the Ibrahim Prize, which pays $200,000 a year for life to African leaders who deliver for citizens and democratically hand over power.

Dos: Go where others refuse to look. Build rules that make your values enforceable.
 Don'ts: Don't accept "that's how business is done here." Don't wait for permission from a bureaucracy.

🎃History of Halloween🎃 

Halloween (the contraction of All Hallows' Eve) dates back to folk customs from Celtic-speaking countries, some of which have pagan roots. Some historians date the origins as far back as the Roman feast of Parentalia, the festival of the dead.

The most accepted origin was the Celtic festival of Samhain, which is Old Irish for 'summer's end'. Samhain was celebrated from October 31 through November 1 in Ireland & Scotland. The festival marked the end of harvest season and beginning of the 'darker half' of the year.

Similar to other cultures, this time of year was seen as when the boundary between this world and the Otherworld thinned, where spirits and fairies could easily come into this world. In 19th century Ireland, candles would be lit and prayers offered for the souls of the dead.

The earliest origins of trick-or-treating was guising in Ireland in the 16th century, where people would go house-to-house in costume (or disguise), reciting verses or songs in exchange for food. This may originate from people impersonating souls of the dead.

The custom of making jack-o'-lanterns at Halloween goes back to Ireland in the 19th century, where turnips tended to be the popular vegetable of choice. The lanterns were said to represent spirits or supernatural beings, even to ward off evil spirits.

The Christian influence on the holiday dates back to the early days of the church, where All Saints' Day (Nov. 1) and All Souls' Day (Nov. 2) were feasts were had to honor saints and pray for the recently departed souls who'd yet reached heaven.

In 835, All Hallows' Day (aka All Saints' Day) was moved to November 1, the same day as Samhain, the Celtic counterpart.

All Hallows' Eve arrived in North America in the southern British colonies and Maryland, though Puritans in New England maintains strong opposition to the holiday, including other celebrations such as Christmas.

It would be in the 19th century, with the arrival of Irish and Scottish immigrants that Halloween became a major holiday in North America. In the over century since, many more activities have become tied to Halloween, such as bobbing for apples, nut roasting, and more.

Today, Halloween is celebrated around the world, spreading beyond its Celtic and Christian origins. Trick-or-Treating, apple bobbing, pranks, and haunted attractions continue to be popular. https://t.co/elcSWgmJQG

text:
The Nueces River Authority (NRA) selected IDE Technologies primarily for its specialized experience building and operating large-scale seawater reverse-osmosis desalination plants, along with its willingness to privately finance and share risk on a project the small public agency could not fund itself.⁠Ide-tech

Stated reasons from NRA officials
Track record: NRA Executive Director John Byrum said IDE “ranked number one in the evaluation by the team.” He highlighted that the company has more than 400 projects worldwide, produces over 1.5 billion gallons of drinking water per day, and has done so for 60 years. Board President Eric Burnett called IDE “the clear, standout choice.”⁠Kiiitv

U.S. operating experience: IDE has long-term involvement with the Carlsbad Desalination Plant in California (one of the largest in the Western Hemisphere when it opened), which NRA and IDE both cite as proof of successful large-scale seawater desalination in the U.S.⁠ Texasedc

Modular design and speed: IDE’s modular approach (manufacturing and assembling major components in phases) was presented as a way to shorten timelines and get water online faster for a drought-stressed region.⁠ Texasedc
 
Private financing and risk-sharing: The NRA is a small agency that lacked the capital for a multi-billion-dollar plant. IDE offered to finance and own/operate the plant (roughly half the ~$6.4 billion total cost) while the public entity handles pipelines. Officials described this as shifting construction and cost-overrun risk away from taxpayers. IDE’s Texas representative Mark Ellison emphasized sharing risk and bringing funding to the table.⁠ Kristv

The selection was unanimous after the board authorized negotiations with IDE as the preferred development partner. This followed an earlier unsolicited proposal path and an evaluation process in which IDE ranked highest.

Context on why not a pure American public project: Texas has pursued large seawater desalination for decades (including under Gov. Rick Perry), but earlier proposals by American firms (such as Poseidon Water, Kiewit, and Seven Seas) often stalled because desalinated water was more expensive than traditional sources and because public projects faced rising cost estimates, political delays, and financing limits. Corpus Christi’s own municipal desalination effort with Kiewit encountered significant cost and timeline problems. The NRA’s private-partner model was chosen in part to avoid those issues and move faster on a very large plant (initially up to 100 million gallons per day).⁠Insideclimatenews

In short, the NRA framed the choice as driven by IDE’s unmatched global scale and experience with plants of this type, plus a financing structure that matched the agency’s limited resources—not by any exclusion of American companies. American firms remain active in Texas desalination (including Aquatech and Kiewit on Corpus Christi’s separate public plant).

Walmart just started selling electricity reliability at the checkout aisle.

On Oct 30, Walmart announced an investment in Base Power, a 2023 Austin startup, plus a deal to offer its home batteries at participating Walmart and Sam's Club stores.

The model is the interesting part. Base installs, owns, and maintains the battery. The customer pays an upfront installation fee, and from November, enrolling through Walmart gets 20% off that fee.

Base already has 35,000+ members in Texas, and 20,000+ of those homes have a Base battery. Texas goes first, with more markets "over time."

The lesson: Walmart isn't building an energy company. It's renting its foot traffic to one that already works.

Would you buy home backup power at a Walmart?

Brazilian coffee, beef and tropical fruit will still be tariffed 40%, says Brazil’s vice president

RIO DE JANEIRO — Brazilian Vice President Geraldo Alckmin said Saturday that Brazilian exported goods to the U.S. including coffee, beef and tropical fruits would still be tariffed 40%, despite President Donald Trump’s decision to remove some import taxes.

In a dramatic move on Friday, Trump scrapped levies announced in April on what he called ‘Liberation Day’ in hopes of encouraging domestic production and lifting the U.S. economy. Brazil at the time was hit with a 10% tariff.

But in July, Trump imposed a further 40% tariff, citing — among other reasons — the trial of his ally, former President Jair Bolsonaro, which he called a “witch hunt.” Proceedings went ahead regardless and in September Bolsonaro was sentenced to 27 years and three months in prison for attempting a coup.

Alckmin said some products, such as orange juice, would now have a zero tariff as they were not targeted by the additional 40%. But that extra tariff remains in place on products including coffee, beef and tropical fruits, such as mangos and pineapples.

While Brazil’s vice president welcomed Trump’s latest decision, which he called “positive” and a “step in the right direction,” he said there remained a “distortion that needs to be corrected.”

“Everyone got 10% less, but in Brazil’s case, which had 50%, we ended up with 40%, which is very high,” Alckmin told journalists in the capital Brasilia.

Alckmin said that Friday's decision means that 26% of Brazilian goods are now entering the U.S. without additional tariffs. That's up from 23%.

Trump’s July decision, which was overtly political as Brazil has a trade deficit with the United States, led to the worst U.S.-Brazil relations in history.

Those relations have since improved, and in October Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Trump met in Malaysia.

“President Lula’s conversation with President Donald Trump was important in terms of dialogue and negotiation,” Alckmin said on Saturday.

After that encounter, Lula said he was confident the two countries would soon reach a trade deal.

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Brazil’s Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira met for 50 minutes this week to further the conversation.

The Trump administration has insisted that its tariffs helped fill government coffers and weren’t a major factor in higher prices at grocery stores around the country. But Democrats were quick to paint Friday’s move as an acknowledgment that Trump’s policies were hurting American pocketbooks.

Record-high beef prices have been a particular concern, and Trump had said he intended to take action to try and lower them. Trump’s tariffs on Brazil, a major beef exporter, had been a factor.

Back in Brazil, the Brazilian Association of the Coffee Industry said it would continue to monitor the situation.

“(We) will keep working to ensure legal certainty, competitiveness, and predictability for the Brazilian coffee industry,” the group’s president, Pavel Cardoso, said in a statement. (Wires, A.I News)

PBBM pushes for key dev't priorities in agriculture, infrastructure, governance
By Ruth Abbey Gita-Carlos 

MANILA – President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. advanced the administration’s development agenda this week, highlighting initiatives to modernize agriculture, improve infrastructure, attract investments, strengthen justice reforms, and promote inclusive governance. 

Through a series of engagements, the President’s week underscored the government’s efforts to translate infrastructure investments, institutional reforms, and economic partnerships into tangible benefits for Filipinos. 

Marcos intensified the government’s efforts to strengthen agricultural productivity and prepare farmers for the anticipated effects of a strong El Niño, emphasizing the importance of reliable irrigation, renewable energy, and climate-resilient farming technologies. 

Sustaining agricultural production 

Marcos on Monday inaugurated the Alfonso Lista Pump Irrigation System in Barangay Sto. Domingo, Alfonso Lista, Ifugao, highlighting the importance of dependable water supply in improving agricultural production and farmers’ livelihoods. 

He assured farmers that the government would continue pursuing initiatives to improve their livelihood, support their families, and strengthen agricultural communities. 

The President also emphasized the need for stronger collaboration among government agencies, local government units, and farmers’ cooperatives to advance agricultural development and ensure food security. 

In Cagayan, Marcos inaugurated the Pamplona Solar Pump Irrigation Project in Barangay Gattu, showcasing the administration’s push for more cost-efficient and climate-resilient irrigation systems. 

The solar-powered facility is expected to irrigate more than 600 hectares of farmland, including an additional 100 hectares that will benefit from a more reliable water supply. 

It could also allow farmers in some areas to increase their cropping cycles from one to two annually. 

The project is expected to significantly reduce farmers’ operating expenses by replacing costly diesel-powered pumps with solar energy. 

Strengthening energy security and water management 

As part of efforts to safeguard the country’s energy and water resources, Marcos visited the Integrated Remote Operations Center of SN Aboitiz Power-Magat, Inc. in Ramon, Isabela. 

During the visit, Marcos was briefed on the proposed Magat Floating Solar Power Project, which aims to expand renewable energy generation while helping reduce water evaporation from the Magat Reservoir. 

The proposed project is expected to supply clean electricity to approximately 42,000 households and generate additional revenue for the National Irrigation Administration to support irrigation services. 

Improving mobility 

Marcos also pushed for improved road connectivity and more efficient transportation as he inaugurated and inspected the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) - C5 Northlink Segment 8.2 Section 1A on Thursday. 

The 2-km. expressway section, which connects Quirino Highway to the NLEX Mindanao Toll Plaza, is expected to cut travel time from approximately 40 minutes to just 5 minutes, benefitting nearly 11,000 motorists daily. 

The new segment provides motorists coming from Quirino Highway direct access to the NLEX Connector, facilitating trips to Manila, the University Belt, and nearby cities. It also offers an alternative route to EDSA, helping ease traffic congestion in Metro Manila. 

Motorists traveling north can use the new section to access the NLEX mainline toward Central Luzon and connect to the Subic-Clark-Tarlac Expressway for trips to Northern Luzon. 

Marcos announced that motorists could use the new section free of charge until the end of the year. 

He also announced a planned PHP120 billion investment by the MPC Group of Companies and the SMC Group for an elevated road project connecting Balintawak to Bocaue. 

The President also received an update on the construction of the Metro Manila Subway Project (MMSP) Depot in Barangay Ugong. 

The PHP143 billion Contract Package 101 covers the construction of the depot, underground tunnels, and four key stations: East Valenzuela, Quirino Highway, Tandang Sora, and North Avenue. 

Boosting local manufacturing and EV industry 

Marcos also highlighted the importance of foreign investments in developing local industries and creating employment opportunities during his visit to the newly inaugurated manufacturing and assembly plant of Sazgar Philippines, Inc. in Biñan City, Laguna. 

He described the investment as a vote of confidence in the Philippines and opportunity to strengthen the country’s position in the growing electric vehicle (EV) manufacturing sector. 

He encouraged Sazgar Philippines to expand its local supply chain, noting that many of its components are still sourced from abroad. 

Marcos also reaffirmed the government’s commitment to supporting the EV industry through the implementation of the Electric Vehicle Industry Development Act. 

Correction reforms and reintegration programs 

Marcos also vowed to improve the country’s correctional system and ensure that qualified persons deprived of liberty (PDLs) received timely legal assistance and opportunities for rehabilitation. 

On Wednesday, the President led the observance of the 32nd National Correctional Consciousness Week at the New Bilibid Prison Reservation in Muntinlupa City. 

He interacted with PDLs and visited elderly inmates, while observing rehabilitation initiatives designed to equip them with practical skills and prepare them for reintegration into society. 

He also reiterated his directive to the Department of Justice to prioritize correctional reforms, strengthen access to legal assistance, and expedite the release of individuals who have completed their sentences and are legally eligible for discharge. 

Upholding judicial integrity 

The President, along with First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, also hosted nearly 160 newly appointed first- and second-level court judges at Malacañan Palace in Manila on Monday. 

He congratulated the judges from different judicial regions and expressed confidence in their competence and ability to serve the country with integrity. 

He urged them to uphold impartiality, accountability, and the highest standards of professionalism in dispensing justice. 

Parliamentary governance 

Marcos also graced the inaugural session of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) Parliament at the Bangsamoro Government Center in Cotabato City on Friday. 

The occasion marked a significant milestone in the region’s transition to regular parliamentary governance following its parliamentary elections on Sept. 14, which elected 80 members of Parliament. 

The first regular Parliament is expected to enact regional laws, approve public spending, and oversee government programs, marking the transition from more than seven years of governance under the Bangsamoro Transition Authority. 

Under Republic Act 11054, or the Bangsamoro Organic Law, the Parliament will elect the Chief Minister through a majority vote of at least 41 members. 

The Chief Minister will lead the regional government and pursue its development priorities, subject to parliamentary oversight. 

Expanding diplomatic and economic partnerships 

As part of his commitment to strengthen international relations, Marcos received the credentials of four non-resident ambassadors at Malacañan on Tuesday. 

The ambassadors represented Jordan, Chad, Fiji, and Burundi, with their accreditation opening opportunities for stronger cooperation in trade, investments, tourism, education, and people-to-people exchanges. 

The President also received Sri Lankan Ambassador Dr. Chanaka Harsha Talpahewa during a farewell call on Wednesday, recognizing his contributions to strengthening bilateral relations. 

Promoting Filipino culinary excellence 

Marcos and the First Lady also attended the Michelin Guide Ceremony of Manila and Environs at the Marriott Hotel in Pasay City on Thursday. 

The event recognized outstanding restaurants through Michelin Stars and Bib Gourmand distinctions, highlighting the country’s growing culinary landscape and the international recognition of Filipino chefs and restaurateurs. 

Returning to the Philippines for its second edition, the Michelin Guide further supports the administration’s efforts to position the country as a world-class culinary destination. 

The President’s engagements throughout the week form part of the broader Bagong Pilipinas agenda, which aims to build a more resilient, competitive, and inclusive nation where the benefits of development reach more Filipinos. (PNA)

text:
Renaissance over revolution; Spinoza over Machiavelli (with important caveats).
Renaissance vs. Revolution
A renaissance is cultural and intellectual renewal—recovering, reinterpreting, and building on earlier achievements while generating new ones. The Italian Renaissance (roughly 14th–16th centuries) revived classical learning, elevated human agency and individualism, advanced art, architecture, and early modern science, and shifted authority toward observation and reason without requiring the wholesale destruction of existing institutions. It was uneven, elite-driven in many respects, and intertwined with political fragmentation and conflict, but its long-term effects were generative rather than purely destructive.
A revolution, in the modern political sense, aims at rapid, structural overthrow of the existing order—often involving mass mobilization, violence, and the claim that the old regime is irredeemable. The American case was relatively restrained and institutionally constructive; the French, Russian, Chinese, and various 20th-century examples frequently produced terror, dictatorship, economic collapse, and ideological rigidity before any lasting gains. Revolutions tend to concentrate power in the hands of those skilled at seizing it, discard accumulated practical knowledge, and replace one set of rulers with another (often more absolute). They can clear space for later improvement, but the body count and institutional wreckage are real costs, not side effects.
Renaissances are usually preferable because they compound knowledge and capacity instead of resetting them. Revolutions are sometimes necessary when institutions are truly ossified or tyrannical and peaceful reform is blocked, but they are high-variance and frequently net-negative.
Machiavelli or Spinoza?
Niccolò Machiavelli (1469–1527) is the sharper diagnostician of power. The Prince and the Discourses treat politics as it is practiced under scarcity, ambition, and contingency: virtù, fortune, the utility of cruelty, the limits of idealism. He is essential for understanding why regimes rise and fall, why republican orders need both civic virtue and hard-headed institutional design, and why moralizing alone does not produce stable order. The common charge that he simply “separates ethics from politics” is overstated; he is more accurately read as showing that political survival has its own constraints that pure ethical systems ignore at their peril. His work remains indispensable for realists.
Baruch Spinoza (1632–1677) offers the more constructive framework for free and rational social life. In the Ethics and the Theologico-Political Treatise, he argues that genuine freedom is understanding the causes that determine us, that democracy is the regime most consistent with preserving the power of the multitude, and that free inquiry and the separation of philosophy from ecclesiastical authority are practical necessities. His geometric method and monism are austere, and he is no utopian about human passions, yet he supplies a positive account of how reason, tolerance, and institutional checks can expand the sphere in which people can act according to their own nature rather than under arbitrary domination. He is deeper on the conditions of lasting liberty and on the relationship between knowledge and power.
Machiavelli is better for diagnosing what must be done to acquire or defend power. Spinoza is better for thinking about the kind of order worth defending and the psychological and institutional conditions that make freedom sustainable. For most purposes of building durable, non-tyrannical societies, Spinoza’s orientation is the more fruitful one; Machiavelli’s tools are still required to implement it.
How the pairs relate
Machiavelli is a Renaissance figure who already sees the limits of pure cultural or humanist optimism; he analyzes the political conditions under which any revival can survive. Spinoza belongs to the subsequent scientific and rationalist

You can blame the climate hysteria Canada and the EU is still enamored with.
Politicians and evening news broadcasts love to tell you that the war in Iran is the sole reason gas prices are sky-high. This is a massive misconception that completely ignores history. ( the only thing we learn from history??….)

The truth is, the United States doesn't even buy oil from Iran. The war only caused a crisis because past government policies had already pushed our fuel system to the absolute edge. 

Let me explain and ask you to consider

When a barrel of crude oil costs $103 today, you pay about $4.35 a gallon at the pump [Fortune]. But 15 years ago, when a barrel of oil cost that exact same $105, gas was only $3.51 a gallon.
So WHY is gas so much more expensive now for the exact same barrel of oil?

The United States is actually the largest oil producer in the entire world, pumping out record-breaking amounts of raw crude oil. But raw oil straight out of the ground is useless—you can't dump it into your car's gas tank. It has to go to a refinery to be cooked and cleaned into gasoline and diesel.

The PROBLEM is that past government administrations fundamentally broke the refining industry. 

Over the last 30 years, Washington politicians passed massive, expensive environmental rules. They didn't directly order refineries to close, but they made running them so expensive that smaller, independent factories couldn't afford to stay open and went out of business. 

On top of that, the government started offering huge tax-credit bribes to big oil companies if they stopped making regular fuel and switched to green biofuels instead.

ARE YOU FOLLOWING?
Because past governments squeezed the industry from both sides, America lost dozens of processing plants. The current remaining refineries are completely redlined, running at 98% capacity with absolutely zero backup plan!!

We have all the raw oil we could ever need, but because past government policies choked off our ability to refine it, those few remaining factories can charge a massive scarcity premium just to turn that cheap oil into gas.

Here’s who to be upset with:

🏭 Bill Clinton (1993–2001)

• The Rule: He passed strict new anti-smog rules that forced factories to make special, complicated fuel mixes for big cities.
• What Happened: Changing the factories was way too expensive. Giant oil companies could afford it, but dozens of smaller, neighborhood gas factories couldn't afford the upgrades and had to close down forever.

🌽 George W. Bush (2001–2009)

• The Rule: He made a law forcing oil companies to mix billions of gallons of corn juice (ethanol) into regular gasoline.
• What Happened: Instead of spending money to build bigger, better oil factories, companies had to spend billions of dollars building special blending tanks and shipping networks just for corn ethanol.

💨 Barack Obama (2009–2017)

• The Rule: He passed aggressive rules forcing factories to clean out almost all the sulfur from gasoline and track all their greenhouse gases.
• What Happened: This created another massive bill for the industry. More small, independent factories couldn't afford the multi-million dollar price tag to meet the new laws, so they shut down or sold out to giant corporations.

🌱 Joe Biden (2021–2026)

• The Rule: He pushed heavily for electric cars and offered giant tax-money rewards (bribes) to companies that made green energy instead of oil.
• What Happened: Oil bosses realized they could make way more money collecting government checks by switching to green fuels. They actively chose to dismantle major traditional gas factories and rebuild them into green biofuel plants, taking massive amounts of regular gas and diesel off the market right before the global crisis hit.

When Bill Clinton took office, the United States had 179 operational petroleum refineries.
Today, that number has dropped to 130 operational refineries in the USA.
This represents a total net loss of 49 refineries.

3 DAYS LEFT TO GO

Washington State mobilizes National Guard for added security for ballot drop boxes

Members will be unarmed and in plainclothes. They will observe and call authorities if they see someone tampering with a box.

** Q. Why are National Guard needed until November 10th?

Oct. 30, 2026

In a precedent-setting move, members of the Washington National Guard are being deployed in seven counties to help protect ballot drop boxes in the final days of the election.

The mission, dubbed Election Neighborhood Watch by Gov. Bob Ferguson, appears to be the first large-scale activation of National Guard members to provide greater security of ballots cast in the state’s mail-in system. Nearly 70% of ballots returned so far arrived from a drop box.

As of Friday afternoon, National Guard members were headed to King, Pierce, Snohomish, Thurston, Clark, Lewis and Island counties. Secretary of State Steve Hobbs, who is also a National Guard member, said this “has not been done before.”

Auditors say they had not detected any credible threats to drop boxes that would prompt a request for the National Guard’s presence. But when the governor offered to provide assistance, several accepted, seizing on the opportunity to amplify their efforts at no cost to their local taxpayers.

“There’s a lot of noise about elections right now,” said Linda Kent, Pierce County’s deputy auditor. “Looking at the broader context, out of an abundance of caution additional resources is not a bad idea.”

Pierce County Auditor Linda Farmer said elections officials whose biggest worry was once power outages are now dealing with “threats against the people who work here and the actual ballots.”

Historically, the Washington National Guard has had different roles related to the election.

Cybersecurity professionals from the guard have been activated to assist with cybersecurity tasks for every election since 2016, according to the governor’s office. 

In 2024, Gov. Jay Inslee activated the guard after a drop box was set on fire in Clark County in southwest Washington. More recently white powder has been sent to offices of numerous elected officials in the state and across the country.

“Amid these recent developments and the highly charged atmosphere of this election, my administration is taking every precaution to ensure that every vote counts and that counties have the resources they need to monitor and respond to potential threats,” Ferguson wrote auditors.

Ferguson signed the activation order Oct. 21. It directs the guard members “to provide public safety and ballot security support” to bolster participating counties’ efforts “to ensure free and fair elections.” Election Neighborhood Watch began Monday and will end at 12:01 a.m. on Tuesday, Nov. 10.

National Guard personnel are to be unarmed and in plainclothes, not their uniforms. They are not to interact with voters or have a conspicuous presence at drop boxes, voting centers or other locations where ballots are getting cast. Their role is to observe. If they see someone trying to tamper with a box or other unusual activity, they are to call 911 or notify local authorities.

In Pierce County, they will be doing a “roving survey” of boxes. There, and in other counties, that will likely mean driving around at night and overnight, making visual checks

“We don’t want anybody camped out,” Farmer said. On election night there will be trained observers on hand to lock up and empty boxes when voting ends at 8 p.m.

King County is taking a similar approach.

“They will simply be additional eyes and ears at drop boxes and Vote Centers, and supplement our existing security plans,” emailed Halei Watkins, communications manager for King County Elections. “This is not intended to be a visible presence, but more folks to say something if they see something.”

Ending Canada’s Double Game

Canada has spent 2026 telling Washington it's a partner while signing deals with Washington's rivals. In January, Mark Carney flew to Beijing and came home with a quota for cheap Chinese electric vehicles at a 6.1 percent tariff, bought with canola relief. In December, Canada became the first non-European partner in the EU's SAFE programme, a €150 billion defence loan facility that steers Canadian procurement toward European suppliers. Ottawa has said the quiet part out loud, it wants to double its non-US exports by 2030.

So Canada wants American market access, American security cover, and a Chinese and European hedge on the side, and it expects the United States to pay for all three. This proposes ending that arrangement for @realDonaldTrump admin to use.

 Three instruments, applied in sequence: a managed cut in US purchases of Canadian crude, a suspension of Canada's privileged access to US dollar liquidity, and a 50 percent reduction in bilateral goods trade. Each comes with an exit tied to specific Canadian commitments on China and the EU.

I propose we get serious about the January China EV and canola deal, Canada joining the EU’s SAFE defence fund, the CUSMA review that ended in annual reviews, and Argus data showing non-US crude exports at 15% of Canada’s total.

The main pressure point choices:

•Oil: a licensing regime with a falling duty-free ceiling. Midwest refiners get a temporary exemption, since they depend almost entirely on Canadian crude.
•Dollar access: suspend the Fed swap line first, and hold the harsher step in reserve as the threat.
•Trade: Section 232 and 301 as the vehicles, with a rebate for US content so GM and Ford aren’t the casualties.
•Conditions: written demands on China, the EU and the bilateral irritants, tied to a 30/90-day sequence.

The pressure ends when Canada does the following, in writing, with verification.

On China. Rescind the EV tariff quota and cancel any approvals for joint ventures with Chinese automakers. Adopt investment screening aligned with US standards for ports, critical minerals, telecom, and battery supply chains. Accept a North American external tariff regime for Chinese-origin content, so CUSMA's rules of origin can't be used as a side door.

On Europe. Withdraw from SAFE or cap Canadian participation so that US defence suppliers aren't displaced in Canadian procurement. Keep CETA, but strip out any rules-of-origin provisions that let Chinese inputs ride into the American market through Canadian or European assembly.

On the bilateral irritants. Open provincial liquor shelves to American products, end the discriminatory digital measures, and make an actual offer on dairy.

The breakthrough localized ceasefire on the Kherson front line has so far held in place, allowing critical humanitarian supplies into the besieged town of Alyoshki, where thousands of residents were facing starvation.

Convoys from Russia carrying food supplies, medicines, sanitary materials and fuel began arriving Friday. The town had been largely cut off from outside contact since May this year. For nearly six months, the people of Alyoshki have been living in extreme deprivation under deadly assault from drones and mines fired by the NATO-backed Ukrainian regime.

Yet the gutter-level Western media have portrayed the suffering of Alyoshki as being caused by Russia.

The plight of the people came to worldwide attention earlier this month when Pope Leo XIV appealed to Russia’s President Vladimir Putin and the Ukrainian side to cooperate on breaking the siege. Then the dire situation facing the town was raised in a phone call between Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump on October 9.

To her credit, America’s First Lady Melania Trump offered assistance in mediating a ceasefire to enable a humanitarian relief mission. It was Melania who announced on October 23 that a truce had been accepted by both sides. The cessation came into effect this week on October 27 at 4 am Moscow time. It is due to end on Sunday at midnight. The window of five days has permitted critical humanitarian supplies for the residents. Buses have also entered the town to evacuate those who want to leave.

Russia’s human rights commissioner Yana Lantratova and her Ukrainian counterpart, Dmitry Lubinets, led a joint mission to deliver aid and oversee arrangements for evacuation.

The relief mission has been a logistical challenge. Alyoshki sits on the left bank of the Dnieper River, facing the city of Kherson on the other bank. Russian troops took Alyoshki (Oleshky in Ukrainian) during the first weeks of the Special Military Operation in March 2022.

 The Kherson Oblast (region) voted in a referendum to join the Russian Federation four years ago, along with the oblasts of Zaporozhye, Donetsk, and Lugansk. But the city of Kherson remains under the control of Ukraine. The four provinces are historically Russian territory, also known as Novorossiya.

Alyoshki residents have been living on the front line in a pitiful crossfire. The conditions worsened after the Kakhovka dam was blown up by the NATO-backed Kiev regime forces using HIMARS rockets in June 2023. The flood destroyed much of the town’s civilian infrastructure and utilities for drinking water, electricity, and heating. Its population dwindled from a pre-war 25,000 to the present estimated 2,000. 

Their situation deteriorated in March 2025, when the Ukrainian forces blew up a major bridge over the Dnieper. That meant all access to the town was by road from the East through Russian-held territory.

Earlier this year, the Ukrainian forces on the right bank of the river intensified the assault on Alyoshki with swarms of drones firing on inhabitants and their houses while dropping hundreds of mines on the town and its exit roads. Residents who were able to escape spoke of the hellish conditions of starvation while under constant threat of being fired on. Several people were killed or maimed by drones as they attempted to scavenge for food.

In previous months, Russian vehicles attempting to bring in food supplies were routinely targeted by the Ukrainian drones. That was how the town ended up living under siege, and its people were facing starvation. It was methodically cut off by the NATO-backed regime.

Rodion Miroshnik, Russia’s foreign ministry envoy, described the situation as a “medieval blockade using modern methods.”

The Kiev regime and the Western news media have gone into overdrive with propaganda. They have accused Russia of blockading the town and “exploiting” the humanitarian crisis. This is peddling incredible lies and doublethink. So, Russian troops who control Alyoshki are shooting at their own supply efforts? There are also other vile lies, such as Russia denying aid to residents unless they accept Russian citizenship.

Yana Lantratova, @yana_lantratova ,
 the Russian human rights commissioner, said anyone who wishes to relocate to Ukraine will be facilitated. All evacuees will have to be transported into Russia as a first step, then, if they wish, be flown to Belarus and from there to Ukraine. 

The circuitous route is because the Ukrainian forces blew up the bridge crossing the Dnieper. Most evacuees have been glad to be received by Russia.

The Western propaganda distortion is similar to the siege of the Zaporozhye Nuclear Power Plant (ZNPP). The civilian nuclear installation has been under the control of Russian forces since 2022 and has been shelled constantly by the Ukrainian side with NATO weapons. Yet the Western media make out that it is the Russian forces that are targeting the ZNPP.

Another confounding fact for the regime and the Western backers is that most of the Alyoshki residents want to remain in place now that humanitarian needs have been met. They are not fleeing to Ukraine.

Praise is due to Melania Trump for getting personally involved in this crisis and helping bring relief to the people of Alyoshki. She said that American journalists have been allowed to observe the humanitarian mission along with their Russian counterparts. The U.S. news crew was said to be from the Newsmax outlet, which tends to be favorable to President Trump in its coverage. Though, notably, before the arrival of the relief mission on Friday, Newsmax anchors were repeating the Western media narrative that the humanitarian crisis had been caused by Russia. It will be interesting to see what its reporters have to say after visiting the town and talking with residents firsthand.

There has been some speculation that the success of the Alyoshki truce could catalyze a wider ceasefire in Ukraine. That’s unlikely. Moscow has consistently said that the solution to the conflict requires a peace settlement dealing with long-term issues of security and NATO’s historic aggression. A temporary general ceasefire is not acceptable.

Nevertheless, what the Alyoshki breakthrough demonstrates is the benefit of dialogue and a basic commitment to cooperate in resolving difficulties. In principle, with that kind of attitude, any problem can be solved, and that’s “the art of the possible,” or diplomacy at work.

text:
A National Guard officer’s greeting to Maria Corina Machado changed nothing, and that is precisely why it deserves attention: transitions are lost when an image is mistaken for an institution.

On October 28, in La Guaira, María Corina Machado was making her way along roads damaged by the June 24 earthquakes. She had been back in Venezuela for three days. A National Guard officer approached her, greeted her, and spoke with her for about ten seconds. Someone recorded the encounter. Within hours, the footage was circulating on social media as though the uniformed officer had bowed before the opposition leader.

That scene changes nothing. No command changed hands, no order was disobeyed, no military barracks declared its allegiance. It was a gesture of courtesy between two people on a street where residents are still waiting for their homes to be rebuilt. Even so, dismissing it as meaningless would be another mistake. Transitions rarely begin with decrees. They begin with images that show a society that another way of behaving is possible.

In Venezuela, two forms of power coexist but do not coincide. One controls the guns, the budgets, the appointments, and the offices. The other enjoys the recognition of millions of people who turned out to welcome Machado on October 25 and who accompany her on every visit. The first commands because it can compel obedience. The second carries weight because people accept its legitimacy. The story of recent years is the distance between these two forms of power. The greeting in La Guaira matters because, for ten seconds, that distance seemed to disappear.

Consider the guard. If he offers a greeting, he risks disciplinary action, a mark on his record, or his career. If he does not, he risks nothing. The calculation made by a public official in a polarized country is not heroic: it is the calculation of someone who feels he could lose what he already has. That is why such a gesture should not be interpreted as an expression of allegiance or an act of disobedience. It raises a question: what would happen if offering a greeting carried no consequences? The answer does not come from the guard. It comes from the rules that protect or punish those who offer such greetings. And in a country where everyone watches everyone else with suspicion, every public gesture is calculated twice: what does the superior see, what does the public see, and what price might be paid tomorrow?

Machado did not go to La Guaira looking for a military barracks. She went to visit earthquake victims. That is the second meaning of her visit: a movement born in the streets wants to become a set of rules that apply to everyone, including those who did not vote for it. That requires something more difficult than mobilizing supporters: treating officials of a state that until yesterday shut its doors to you with respect, without asking them to betray their uniforms, but rather to uphold the law. No one takes the first step if they distrust what the other side will do tomorrow. That is why gestures are not enough, written, public, and verifiable agreements are needed.

Each media outlet framed the visit in its own way. Some focused on the greeting. Others highlighted residents’ questions about reconstruction. Both portrayals are accurate, and both are incomplete. The image of the greeting says one thing: a guard greets a political leader. It suggests another: respect and peaceful coexistence. And it tempts people to tell a third story: that reconciliation between civilians and the military has already taken place. That third story is a myth, and the myth is dangerous because it allows people to celebrate a transition that does not yet exist. Images of peaceful coexistence, on the other hand, undermine the narrative that everything must be confrontation. That is their real value, and also their limitation.

We must distinguish between different levels, just as we distinguish between having the key and owning the house. Machado has the support of the people in the streets, but she does not control the treasury, the appointments, or the signature that moves an administrative file forward. A greeting hands over none of those keys. Nor does it take them away. What it does is show that, for a moment, the door was not closed.

From here on, there are three possible paths, and none is predetermined. The first is that everything remains the same: the greeting becomes an anecdote, and the rules do not change. The second is that a small opening emerges: greater guarantees for civil interactions and public signs of neutrality. The third is that the laws, oversight mechanisms, and training change. Only the third constitutes a transition. The other two are simply waiting under better lighting.

Meanwhile, each actor operates according to a different timetable. Washington is watching the November 3 electoral calendar and calling for a new Supreme Court before the end of the year and an Electoral Council afterward, without yet setting a date for voting. Delcy Rodríguez’s interim government administers and negotiates, needing the process to move forward without losing control. Machado mobilizes supporters and demands guarantees, but she does not sign appointments. The Armed Forces protect their discipline and institutional continuity. None of these timetables matches that of La Guaira’s earthquake victims, who measure time in homes that have yet to be rebuilt.

The United States is currently calling the shots in the process. That brings both an advantage and a risk. The advantage is that no one else can impose a timetable on a government that has spent years pushing deadlines further into the future. The risk is that outside supervision becomes the norm: Washington manages the deadlines, Caracas manages the waiting, and democracy is always postponed until the next phase. First, prevent everything from collapsing; then rebuild; and finally, hold elections. The sequence sounds reasonable until one notices that the third phase never arrives.

That is why the right question is not whether the guard sympathizes with Machado. Nobody knows, and it does not matter. There are five questions that matter, and all must be answered with facts, not photographs. Are the same protocols applied to political leaders of every persuasion? Is an officer punished for greeting an opposition figure? Have the doctrine, training, and oversight of the security forces changed? Are abuses investigated independently, and is professionalism rewarded as firmly as misconduct is punished? Can Parliament genuinely exercise oversight over the uniformed services? As long as the answers to those questions remain no, La Guaira will be an anecdote, not a turning point.

There is another level that almost nobody examines: the middle ranks, the officers who connect orders from above with the streets below. Their training, salaries, and legal protections determine whether a reform is implemented or shelved. A guard offering a greeting is the first rung of a four-rung ladder: the gesture, the permission, the rule, and the Constitution. The greeting barely reaches the first. A transition is not brought about by a single leader. It is achieved by a network: judges, parliament, military commanders, and citizens who exercise oversight.

Ultimately, the measure of change will not be how many military personnel greet a political leader. It will be whether any Venezuelan, Chavista or opposition supporter, can approach a uniformed official with the same guarantees. On October 28, in La Guaira, an image suggested that this is possible. Images do not bring about transitions. Institutions are built after the cameras are turned off do. Venezuela will know it has crossed that threshold on the day a greeting like this is no longer news.

"Ten Seconds in La Guaira, Venezuela"
By Antonio de la Cruz (El Nacional)

"No one wants to touch it." American companies refuse to buy Russian diesel.

Shipments of Russian diesel, which were supposed to arrive in the United States as part of a deal between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, have been offered to American companies for several weeks, but none of them have yet agreed to become buyers, according to sources in the energy industry and analysts who spoke to The Washington Sun.

The Trump administration is trying to persuade businesses to participate in the deal. But everyone is trying to stay as far away from it as possible, a trader from Wall Street told the newspaper, citing conversations with representatives of leading energy companies: "No one wants to get involved in this, because they are afraid of what will happen in the next session of Congress. No one wants to get caught up in a long legal battle or a series of investigations."

🇮🇱 Palestinian Lawmaker Says Arab Parties Ready to Support Eisenkot Government to End Netanyahu’s Rule

🗳️ Arab Parties Offer Political Cooperation: Palestinian Israeli lawmaker Ahmad Tibi says Arab parties are prepared to support a minority government led by opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, arguing that political cooperation is essential to ending Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s rule following Israel’s inconclusive parliamentary election.

🏛️ Historic Election Results: Final results show Netanyahu’s political bloc securing 53 seats, Eisenkot’s opposition alliance winning 48 seats, and Arab parties capturing a historic 19 seats in Israel’s 120 member Knesset. Neither major bloc has reached the 61 seats required for a parliamentary majority.

🤝 Support Without Joining Government: Tibi emphasized that the Arab Joint List is willing to support an Eisenkot administration from outside the governing coalition without demanding ministerial positions. Such an arrangement could allow Eisenkot to establish a minority government while maintaining cooperation with Arab lawmakers on crucial parliamentary votes.

⚖️ Conditions for Cooperation: Arab representatives want commitments to address rising crime in Arab communities, halt home demolitions in Bedouin towns, increase public investment, and strengthen equality for Palestinian citizens of Israel.

🚨 Eisenkot Faces Political Resistance: Despite the offer, Eisenkot has previously rejected forming a government with Arab parties, citing political and ideological differences. Some members of his opposition alliance also oppose relying on Arab parliamentary support, creating significant obstacles to negotiations.

🔴 Netanyahu Challenges Arab Electoral Gains: Netanyahu and his Likud party have alleged voting irregularities involving Arab parties. Election officials have said there is no evidence that the integrity of the election was systematically compromised, although specific allegations remain under investigation.

🔍 Potential Path to Ending Netanyahu’s Government: The combined 67 seats held by Eisenkot’s alliance and the Arab parties represent a parliamentary majority outside Netanyahu’s bloc. However, those parties have not agreed to govern together. Reports that the ultra Orthodox United Torah Judaism party might also consider supporting an Eisenkot minority administration have introduced another possible route to a change in government, although no agreement has been finalized.
