text:
Fact Check: “Democrat insiders promised David Crowley $250,000 and a job for his wife in a Sara Rodriguez administration to get him out of the governor's race. He took the deal, exited the race, and endorsed Rodriguez the next [day].”

Bottom line: Unproven allegation.

Here's what can be verified:
✅ David Crowley did withdraw from the Wisconsin Democratic gubernatorial primary in July 2026 and endorsed Sara Rodriguez the following day. Multiple news outlets reported both the withdrawal and immediate endorsement. [https://t.co/DxKSTdDs7j], [https://t.co/SmM75VTXoN], [wisconsine...aminer.com]
✅ A report by the Daily Wire alleged that a Democratic insider claimed Crowley agreed to leave the race in exchange for a promised $250,000 and a job for his wife in a future Rodriguez administration. The report says it relied on an unnamed party operative and "corroborating materials." [https://t.co/TEHYKa1pxz]
✅ Subsequent reports stated that an anonymous Democratic adviser allegedly signed an affidavit making similar claims. Those reports said the affidavit's authenticity was verified, meaning the affidavit exists and was signed. However, they did not establish that the alleged deal actually occurred. [https://t.co/KwbqJbJf0f], [https://t.co/rVYhIqjroq]
✅ Reports also note that the Crowley campaign denied the allegations. [https://t.co/KwbqJbJf0f], [wisconsinr...ghtnow.com], [https://t.co/rVYhIqjroq]

❌ There is currently no publicly available evidence showing that:

$250,000 was actually transferred,
a job was actually promised or offered,
Crowley accepted such a deal,
Rodriguez approved or participated in such an arrangement.
The sources reporting the allegation rely primarily on anonymous or unnamed insiders and have not published conclusive documentary proof establishing that the alleged agreement occurred. [https://t.co/TEHYKa1pxz], [https://t.co/KwbqJbJf0f], [https://t.co/rVYhIqjroq]

Verdict
Partly True / Unproven

True: Crowley exited the race and endorsed Rodriguez shortly afterward. [https://t.co/DxKSTdDs7j], [https://t.co/SmM75VTXoN], [wisconsine...aminer.com]

Unproven: The claim that he did so because Democratic insiders promised him $250,000 and a job for his wife remains an allegation, not an established fact. The existence of allegations and even a sworn affidavit does not by itself prove the underlying claim. [https://t.co/KwbqJbJf0f], [https://t.co/rVYhIqjroq]

A careful, evidence-based version would be:
"A Democratic insider alleged that David Crowley was offered $250,000 and a job for his wife in exchange for dropping out and endorsing Sara Rodriguez. Crowley and Rodriguez's camp deny the allegation, and no public evidence has independently verified that the alleged deal occurred." [https://t.co/TEHYKa1pxz], [https://t.co/KwbqJbJf0f], [https://t.co/rVYhIqjroq]

The Tribe - Part 5

Alliance

Rowena, the famously beautiful daughter of Hengist, sailed with the relief fleet. She was young, cunning, and absolutely committed to her father.  Soon after her arrival, Hengist arranged a great feast, and invited Vortigern and his leading nobles.  Rowena would spend the evening charming their guests and serving them copious amounts of wine and ale.  She paid considerable attention to Vortigern himself, and the king became enamored with her.  So much so in fact, that he asked for Rowena’s hand in marriage, and promised Hengist whatever he wished in return.

Following the feast, Hengist consulted with the Elders amongst the Saxons of Thanet.  The island was indeed getting crowded, yet few wished to leave as this new land promised much in the way of wealth and opportunity.  If anything the “Saxons” desired to expand.  Hengist sent word to Vortigern, and offered Rowena’s hand in marriage in exchange for Kent.  Vortigern agreed and Rowena became Vortigern’s second wife who he loved fiercely by all accounts.

Following the wedding, Saxons began settling in Kent, while Hengist and Horsa consolidated their hold on the new land.  For the Britons that wanted the Saxons to leave Thanet, they now saw instead even more of their lands given away to an increasing number of the foreigners.  Vortigern, their own Christian King even went so far as to forsake his wife and marry one of these pagan Saxons.  One can only imagine how Vortigern’s children felt about it.  The situation was at a boiling point.  Hengist took full advantage.  He entered directly into Vortigern’s household guard as chief advisor, and promised to protect his son and law the King, boasting that his people were “Stong, fierce, and born for war”.

But open conflict between the Saxons and the Britons who they relied on materially was not wise.  Hengist shrewdly offered Voritgern a solution that would re-direct all the simmering unease and potential violence outside of the realm, while at the same time providing for the Angles and Saxons whose upkeep the Britons now found too expensive.  

Hengist and his warriors would sail north of the Roman wall, into the land of the Picts and Scots.  He would be joined by an invasion fleet from the mainland led by his son Oisc.  Together they would invade the highlands, and avenge the suffering the Britons had endured for decades.  Vortigern agreed, and when Oisc arrived Hengist set sail with a combined fleet of 40 ships…

text:
Scientists put a dead chicken in a forest. Vultures gathered, then a carnivore lunged out of the trees | Discover Wildlife https://t.co/RUABpQCaFR
Writing in the Journal of Raptor Research, the scientists interpret the carnivore’s direct lunging posture as evidence of an opportunistic predation attempt. If that interpretation is correct, the encounter would be the first documented case of a greater grison trying to prey on a turkey vulture.

Most documented cases of vulture predation occur at nests, affecting eggs and nestlings; records involving adults are much rarer. “Few records involve adult vultures, likely because of their strong flight abilities and use of communal roosts,” say the authors in the study. That said, adult turkey vultures are not invulnerable, with a number of documented predation events in the Americas involving large raptors such as bald eagles and golden eagles, mammals such as raccoons and jaguars, and reptiles such as boa constrictors. 

The latest case was observed during a study on scavengers in Jama-Coaque Reserve, a private reserve in Ecuador’s Tumbes–Chocó–Magdalena biodiversity hotspot. As part of the study, the researchers placed a chicken carcass on the ground next to a tree and set up a camera trap in front of it.

The camera-trap images show three adult turkey vultures perched on the roots of the tree before a grison emerges from the undergrowth and lunges at them. The turkey vultures immediately take flight, along with a nearby black vulture. The grison then remains on the roots for around one minute, sniffing around the vultures’ perch, before disappearing out of shot.

The team believe this is the first known case of a direct attack attempt by a greater grison on a vulture. So, why did it do it?

“We ruled out the possibility of kleptoparasitism [where one animal steals food or prey from another] because the experimental carcass had been completely consumed before the recording began,” say the researchers. “Additionally, the grison showed no interest in the remains (bones and feathers) present at the site.”

Could the attack have been territorial? Greater grisons have previously been documented acting aggressively towards raptors during food consumption. Other mustelids (a family of carnivorous mammals to which the greater grison belongs) in Africa, such as the African striped weasel and the honey badger, are also known to confront larger species while displaying strong territoriality. However, in this instance, the researchers could neither prove nor disprove whether the attack was territorial because they were unable to gather additional photographic records of the grison in the area.

The researchers suggest that living in groups helped the vultures detect the threat and escape together, likely preventing the grison from pinning down a target. “Although group formation in vultures may increase competition for food, it also provides antipredator benefits by enhancing collective vigilance and reducing attack success… In our recorded case, group size likely improved vigilance and triggered the simultaneous flight of all individuals, making this strategy effective against potential predators.”

This rare encounter offers a glimpse of vulture foraging and vigilance strategies, as well as the behaviour of carnivores such as the greater grison. It also highlights how camera traps can reveal interactions that might otherwise go unseen – observations that contribute to understanding how food webs work in highly threatened ecosystems.

In the final chapter of this week's Torah portion, "Vayera," is Gen. 22, the Akeida, which means the binding of Isaac. Sometimes people wonder, how could God give His only Son to suffer a gruesome death. He did it for us, because of His great love, and Yeshua as the Son was willing to do it for the same reason. 

The akeida is an event that points to the suffering Messiah. God brought forth a miracle child, Isaac, born of a barren 90 yr old woman; and then commanded that very same miracle child to be sacrificed upon an altar. This is a prophetic teaching that points to Yeshua an even greater miracle child, born of a virgin, who is Savior of Mankind through His own shed blood.  In the Akeida we see the Father’s plan to give His own son as the sacrifice for the sins of the world.
· Gen. 22:2 - "Take your son, your only son, Isaac, whom you love." Like Isaac with Abraham, Yeshua is God's only begotten Son whom He loves. Abraham as the father is called to sacrifice his only son, whom he loves.  Isaac is called to give his life, which he was willing to do. God called it off, but left us with this prophetic picture of what He as the Father was going to do with His own Son for the salvation of Mankind.
· Mount Moriah, where the Akeida takes place, is the exact spot of the Temple mount, where Solomon built the Temple (See, 2 Chron 3:1), and where Yeshua’s throne will rest for all eternity.
· "Offer him there as an “olah” (“burnt offering”).  An olah offering is a kind of offering that happened every day in the Temple, twice per day, so that there was always upon the altar blood to make atonement for sin.  
· 22:6.  “Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and placed it on his son Isaac.”  Abraham had brought a donkey, but nonetheless, he lays the wood upon Isaac.  Why not let the donkey haul the wood? Because here is Isaac, wood on his back, carrying his burden up through Jerusalem to the top of the hill, to die as a sacrifice.  Yeshua was marched through the same city, bearing a wooden cross upon his back, on his way to be crucified as a sacrifice for the sins of mankind.
· 22:7,8:  “The fire and wood are here,” Isaac said, “but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?”  And Abraham answered, “God himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.”  Abraham was speaking prophetically of the Lamb of God, which God Himself would provide.
· 22:13,14 – “A ram caught in a thicket” – The ram was sacrificed instead of Isaac, because the horns of the ram, the shofar, represents the coming of the Messiah King, who is heralded by the sound of the shofar blast.
· 22:14 – “And Abraham called the place ‘Adonai Yireh’ ” (The Lord will see).  For it was revealed to Abraham that God would see for Himself a sacrifice.
There are many portions in the Torah that point to the suffering Messiah. Few are more revealing than the Akeida, concerning God’s plan to save the world thru His only begotten Son, the sacrifice Lamb, Yeshua HaMashiach.  Upon the very mountain where Abraham stood ready to give up Isaac, the Lord will set up His throne forever.  He will establish His reign over the earth in Jerusalem, from Mt. Moriah for all eternity. text:
THE ETERNAL HAS ALWAYS LIVED WITHIN US

At the heart of every trembling soul lie two primal fears: the ache of losing what we cherish and the longing for what eludes us. These fears, universal and timeless, anchor much of our human experience. Yet, the solution to both is deceptively simple yet profoundly transformative: to fall madly, wildly, tenderly in love with this moment—this imperfect, fleeting, sacred now.  

In time, we see the truth hidden beneath life’s glittering promises. The lovers we clung to, the careers we built brick by brick, the faiths that cradled us, the treasures we hoarded, the applause and accolades, even the temple of our own body—all these things, radiant as they seem, cannot deliver the eternal bliss we secretly yearn for. Each one offers, at best, a fleeting taste of happiness before slipping through our fingers like sand.  

This reckoning, this "disillusionment", often arrives unbidden, like a thief in the night, stealing away the sweet illusions of youth. It may knock us to our knees, cloaked as despair, anxiety, midlife regret, or the gnawing hunger of addiction. 

Yet, what a glorious thief it is! For in the rubble of our illusions lies an unassuming treasure—a sacred invitation to step beyond the fleeting pleasures of the world, beyond the gilded promises that never truly delivered, and to remember what we have always been: unchanging, boundless, whole.  

When the mirage dissolves, clarity emerges. No person, possession, potion pinnacle, grand revelation, or fleeting moment of glory has ever held the power to grant us the happiness we seek. This humbling yet profound realization reveals a deeper truth: if no thing can make us happy, happiness must reside in nothing. It must reside within us—in the quiet, luminous presence beneath all wanting.  

And here, at last, we stumble upon the paradox of life. Every heartbreak, every triumph, every mundane morning holds the key to joy not because of what it brings, but because of the infinite grace it reveals within. Nothing can make us happy; that is the most liberating, exhilarating, breathtaking truth. If happiness cannot be found in the fleeting, it must dwell in the eternal and the eternal has always lived within us.  

So laugh at the absurdity of it all, weep for the beauty of it, and rise. Rise, knowing you have never been lost. Your home is here, now, in the infinite embrace of this very moment. The search is over; the treasure is you.  

✨🙌🏾💫

text:
Pestilence and starting Johanka's DLC

You need to finish In God's Hands and Pestilence before Johanka's DLC starts. They can end successfully or unsuccessfully. Warhorse's own instructions say that, so failing to save someone doesn't automatically lock you out of her story. You also don't have to finish Theresa's separate story first. Warhorse's DLC instructions (https://t.co/ZFXH2WUlNm)

Pestilence has another timer to watch. Warhorse's patch notes give the quest a six-day failure time, but they don't say every patient is guaranteed to live that long or spell out the exact conversation that starts it. Don't use that as six days to go do other quests. Warhorse patch notes (https://t.co/aAszuLi4EZ)

Learning to read beforehand lets Henry help with the diagnosis and brew the medicine himself. Nicodemus can also succeed, so reading isn't a confirmed requirement for Plague Doctor, but it lets you get on with the work sooner. Pestilence reference (https://t.co/7w8tXyrDw6)

1. Talk to Matthias and Melichar in Merhojed. Check the sick households before you leave: Melichar's, Vincent's, Daniel's, Bedrishka's and Straw's. Ask about the symptoms. If you're helping Bedrishka bury her husband, dig the grave before moving him. Avoid getting into a fight with Straw. Village investigation (https://t.co/7w8tXyrDw6)

2. Go to Johanka, then Nicodemus. Tell him about the sick villagers and the animals. If Henry can read, examine the medical book and identify poisoned water as the problem. Offer to make the medicine. Diagnosis walkthrough (https://t.co/sOr3bhwwRa)

3. Brew Remedy for Merhojed. Use water, two thistle, one valerian and one charcoal. Boil the thistle for two turns. Add the valerian and boil for one more. Let it cool, add the charcoal, and bottle it without boiling again. Remedy recipe (https://t.co/6bpfvfmvgi)

4. Return to Nicodemus in Straw's house. Give medicine to Daniel, Vincent and Bedrishka. Nicodemus and Johanka handle the other households, but check Straw's wife yourself and use any medicine option that's there. Guides disagree on whether you always have to give her a dose manually, so check rather than walking past her. Treatment instructions (https://t.co/7w8tXyrDw6), additional walkthrough (https://t.co/6bpfvfmvgi)

5. Treat the prisoner too. Ask Melichar for access, give the captive the remedy, and let him recover before questioning him. Once everyone's been treated, come back later and talk to Melichar about the village's recovery. That's when you can check whether you got Plague Doctor. Prisoner and recovery (https://t.co/sOr3bhwwRa)

If the prisoner dies, you can still continue the main story using the letter on his body. Keep your earlier save if you're trying to save everyone. Questions and Answers (https://t.co/5TyD6T3hPr)

Matthias being sick at Sasau later doesn't mean you missed giving him a separate dose here. His illness continues into Johanka's story. Matthias (https://t.co/N5k8Wgf0ds)

Once both quests have ended, return to Johanka at Sasau. If the DLC conversation isn't there, check that both quests really have ended, that she's back from Merhojed, and that the DLC is enabled.

Infernal Dream

Ask Johanka about her dreams and agree to investigate. You're heading to the mines west of Skalitz. Look in the northwestern group of mine entrances; the dead rider and horse nearby help you find the right one.

Take a torch, go through the tunnel and examine the bodies at the end. Then come back out and climb the hill to the shaft above them. Inspect the blood and follow it to the huts.

Save before you approach the man dressed as a Skalitz soldier. Talk to him if you want to hear what he's been doing, then deal with the fight. Search him and the hut before going back to Johanka. When you report what happened, she'll want you to accompany her to the marketplace for her speech the next morning. Infernal Dream walkthrough (https://t.co/nOwqwXJN1s)

For Infernal Justice, pick up the murderer's body and drop it down the vertical shaft where he put his victims. Killing him alone doesn't unlock it. Be careful at the edge so Henry doesn't go down with him. Infernal Justice (https://t.co/I9zQXG7KgP)

Casting Lots: Ambrose and Guta

After Johanka's speech, talk to Guta about Ambrose. Promise you'll give the money back, then find him at the Wagoners' Inn. Talk to him once about what's going on, then again to start drinking. Save before that second conversation.

You need him drunk enough to play dice while Henry can still stay conscious. How much Henry can drink depends on his Drinking skill and perks, so a fixed number of drinks won't work the same for everyone.

One way through the dice games is to bet 12 groschen and lose, bet 60 and win, then persuade him to keep playing. Bet 120 and lose, then get him to wager everything and win that last game. After you've taught him the lesson, give the money back. Casting Lots walkthrough (https://t.co/SS3LpLy5Pb)

Another guide gets him to the all-in wager by losing two games first. You can also outdrink him if Henry's Drinking is high enough, take his money when he passes out, and speak to him when he's sober the next morning. Give it back, report to Guta, and take his dice to throw down the well. Ambrose alternatives (https://t.co/2OJaIuXAjK)

There's disagreement about whether keeping the dice actually hurts the ending. Throwing them away avoids having to depend on that. Dice reference (https://t.co/swYgF2KzjX)

You had one job! requires Henry to pass out drinking with Ambrose. If you want it, choose the heavier drinks, get the achievement, then reload and help him properly. Some guides say you can't do it above Drinking 10, but players report getting it at 11–13 with different perks and some alcohol already in them. Low tolerance makes it easier; that level 10 cutoff isn't reliable. Blackout achievement reports (https://t.co/orGnlQpGhH)

text:
Kidney Transplant Patients Free From Lifelong Medication: Breakthrough Treatment Successful in the US

A new protocol called "Delayed Tolerance" developed at the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA), has successfully freed several kidney transplant recipients from taking lifelong anti rejection medications. The program is led by Dr. Jeffrey Veale, with details published by UCLA Health. Typically, every kidney transplant recipient must take daily medications for the rest of their life to prevent the body from rejecting the organ. However, these drugs carry severe side effects, including an increased risk of infections, diabetes, and cancer.
The key feature of this new approach is its timing. Traditional methods required donor stem cells to be infused on the exact same day as the transplant. Under this new program, months or even years after the surgery once the patient has fully recovered stem cells from the original donor are administered via an IV drip following a mild conditioning regimen. These cells retrain the recipient's immune system to recognize the new kidney as part of the body rather than an foreign object. Over the course of about a year, the immunosuppressive drugs are gradually tapered off until they are completely stopped. Remarkably, this entire process is performed on an outpatient basis.
So far, six patients have participated in the program. Three are completely drug free with the first patient having gone nearly 26 months without any medication. Two others are currently tapering off their drugs, and all participants have stable kidney function with no signs of rejection. Among them is patient Karina Ledesma, who received a kidney from her sister Rosa and has now stopped taking all anti rejection drugs. UCLA is the first center in the world to offer this procedure to patients who have already received a transplant. To advance this research, the California Institute for Regenerative Medicine awarded a $6.7 million grant, and in 2026, the study is expanding to include patients who received their transplants up to 20 years ago.
However, the treatment does have clear limitations. Currently, it is only available to patients who received a kidney from a highly compatible sibling, and it remains in the small-scale clinical trial phase. Most importantly, kidney transplant recipients must never stop taking their medications based on this news, as abruptly discontinuing anti-rejection drugs can lead to organ failure within days. Medications can only be safely discontinued under strict medical supervision within a specialized program like this one. Nevertheless, this breakthrough marks a significant first step toward a future where kidney transplants no longer come with the burden of lifelong medication.

text:
“Hold my beer.”
— UC Irvine

UC Irvine has far more Chinese students by volume and more formal institutional research ties that have drawn congressional scrutiny; Stanford has fewer students but higher-visibility cases of direct targeting of individuals involved in sensitive research, due to its elite status and Silicon Valley location.

—

1. Student numbers

UC Irvine: China is by far the largest source of international students. Open Doors data for Fall 2024 listed roughly 3,733 Chinese students out of about 7,130 total international students. New undergraduate Chinese enrollments have been high (hundreds per year, often 60–70%+ of international new students in recent UC system data). Total Chinese students on campus are typically in the several thousands. It has a large Chinese Students and Scholars Association (CSSA) that has described itself as recognized by the Chinese Embassy.

Stanford: Much smaller absolute numbers. A 2025 Stanford Review investigation cited approximately 1,129 Chinese international students on campus. New undergraduate Chinese admits are low (often in the teens to low dozens in recent years) because of extreme selectivity. Total university enrollment is around 18,000; international students make up a substantial share overall, but Chinese students are a smaller slice than at UCI.

—

UCI is a high-volume public campus heavily reliant on Chinese international students for tuition revenue. Stanford is a small, highly selective private university where Chinese students are concentrated in high-prestige programs.

—

2. Influence operations and documented concerns

Both campuses operate in an environment shaped by China’s National Intelligence Law (which obliges Chinese citizens to assist state intelligence work), CSSAs (frequently described as vectors for monitoring and United Front activity), and the China Scholarship Council (CSC). Differences appear in scale and type of risk.

Stanford has seen more publicized cases of direct targeting of individuals:

Elsa Johnson (Stanford Review editor, East Asian studies major who researched Chinese industry/military topics at the Hoover Institution) was contacted in 2024 by a man posing as a fellow student (“Charles Chen”). He offered a paid trip to China, pressed for personal details, and moved conversations to WeChat. The FBI later assessed he had no real Stanford affiliation, had targeted multiple female students since around 2020, and was likely linked to the Ministry of State Security. Johnson reported subsequent harassment, Mandarin-language intimidation calls, and physical surveillance of her and her family on campus. She testified before the House Committee on Education and the Workforce in March 2026 and has described limited institutional support from Stanford.

The May 2025 Stanford Review investigation (involving Johnson) alleged a broader campus pattern: Chinese students reporting research progress (especially in AI, robotics, and related fields) to handlers, CSC-linked funding as a control mechanism, and overall intelligence-gathering. Stanford’s location next to Silicon Valley and strength in frontier tech make it a high-value target. The House Select Committee on the CCP has also sought detailed data on Chinese students at Stanford and other schools.

UC Irvine shows more volume-driven and structural risks:

In July 2025, the House Select Committee on the CCP wrote to UCI’s chancellor expressing concern about a joint CSC program that sponsors up to 15 PRC graduate students per year for research in the Samueli School of Engineering (12–48 months). The letter noted that CSC students have participated in U.S. government-funded projects (including Department of Energy fusion work involving PRC aerospace-linked entities and blacklisted supercomputing work), and that CSC rules typically require return to China for at least two years. UCI provides tuition support, health insurance, and stipends/assistantships for these students.

UCI has maintained or promoted partnerships with Chinese institutions appearing on U.S. government restricted lists (e.g., a joint mechanical engineering program with Dalian University of Technology, flagged under Department of Defense Section 1286 lists for national-security risks). Broader congressional letters have also raised questions about financial transactions and research collaborations with entities of concern.

The large Chinese student population and active CSSA, combined with Irvine’s sizable Chinese-American community, create a denser environment for influence activities. Recent regional cases (e.g., an Irvine resident charged as an unregistered Chinese agent for surveilling a relative of Taiwan’s president) illustrate the broader Southern California context.

—

3. Bottom line

UC Irvine has greater raw numbers of Chinese students and more explicit institutional research/scholarship pipelines that have attracted formal congressional warnings about technology transfer and military-civil fusion risks. Stanford has fewer Chinese students but faces more visible, high-profile individual targeting and student-reported espionage activity tied to its elite research profile and location. Both fit broader patterns of CCP-linked influence, monitoring, and talent/research acquisition on U.S. campuses; neither is an outlier in California. Public reporting and congressional attention have been stronger around Stanford’s individual cases in recent years, while UCI’s concerns have centered more on structured programs and partnerships.

​1️⃣ Section 197 & Schedule V Caps: Under Indian corporate law, managerial remuneration for loss-making/inadequate profit companies is strictly capped by statutory limits, requires Nomination & Remuneration Committee (NRC) approval, and mandates a Special Resolution passed by public institutional shareholders. A founder cannot arbitrarily "bump salary to ₹75 Cr". His current salary is ~₹6–7 Cr.
  
​2️⃣ Strict Monitoring of Rights Issue Proceeds: SEBI (ICDR) regulations mandate an independent Monitoring Agency (like CARE / CRISIL / Banks) and quarterly reporting to audit every single rupee of the ₹1,000 Cr. Rights capital is tied strictly to the stated objects of the offer (Capex, cell manufacturing, debt repayment)—it cannot legally be routed into executive pay.
  
​3️⃣ Personal Guarantee & Pledge: The promoter personally guaranteed the loan and pledged his own equity. If the tech and business turnaround falter, his own shares get liquidated.
  
​Armchair WhatsApp theories are easy; read the statutory disclosures before inventing corporate fraud! 📊⚖️

text:
Why the "Death" of the AI Agent Harness Is the Best Thing to Happen to Software — Jediah Katz, SpaceXAI

In early 2023, "prompt engineer" was the hottest job title in tech. By mid-2025, the industry had graduated to "context engineer"—someone who programmatically assembles the right context for a model on the fly—and by the start of this year, builders finally landed on "harness engineering" to describe the digital eyes and hands that wrap around an AI model, steer its behavior, and connect it to computers and third-party services. Yet only a few months after Cursor hit "peak harness" by using a massive, expensive multi-model harness called "grind swarm" to build a web browser from scratch, a new consensus swept across tech circles: smarter models have officially killed the agent harness.

When Jediah Katz—the longest-tenured engineer on Cursor's agent harness team, who recently joined SpaceX through its acquisition of Cursor—took the stage to address this debate, he offered a fascinating look behind the curtain. The agent harness is not dead; rather, while the old coding-patch harness is fading, the broader agent harness is more vital than ever for two key reasons: it unlocks the next unmastered frontier of agentic work, and it provides the operational infrastructure, security, and cost efficiency that raw models can never natively absorb.

1. The Old Coding-Patch Harness Was Designed to Put Itself Out of Business

Not long ago, frontier models struggled to apply code edits to files, explore a codebase effectively, or run tests to verify their work. To compensate, harness engineers built elaborate guardrails, coding-specific instructions, and even small helper models just to patch over gaps in raw model intelligence. Recently, however, leaders at Anthropic, Y Combinator, and Cursor itself noticed they were ripping those very system prompts and guardrails out of their codebases as models grew smarter.

   "It turns out the harness is actually making itself obsolete through what I call the data flywheel."

What looks to outsiders like the death of the harness is actually a self-obsoleting feedback loop doing its job. When a harness patches a model's weaknesses, it brings harder coding tasks within reach for everyday users. As more users productively tackle complex problems with agents, more coding data is shared with AI labs, who train the next generation of models to natively absorb those skills—like persistent work and test verification—into their baseline muscle memory. The old coding-patch harness isn't fading because it failed; its temporary scaffolding is disappearing because it succeeded.

2. Reason #1 the Broader Harness Is Vital: Unlocking the Next Frontier of Work

If smarter models have absorbed basic coding tricks, why do we still need harness innovation in the context and orchestration layer? Because the moment a model commoditizes one capability, the broader harness steps up to unlock the next frontier of tasks and kick off the data flywheel all over again.

We can see this happening in two distinct ways as software moves beyond one-off coding chats:

Autonomous Knowledge Work: When the team built Grokbot—an autonomous colleague designed for general knowledge work—they found themselves adding prompts and guardrails right back into the harness. Instead of handling single chat turns, Grokbot relies on long-lived coordinator bots that orchestrate fleets of worker agents.

Multi-Agent "Software Factories": Even within software engineering, the more senior an engineer gets, the less pure coding they actually do. Emerging "meta-harnesses" use entire agents as their core building blocks to orchestrate the full development lifecycle: auto-triaging a bug reported in a chat channel, spinning up a cloud agent to fix the bug and record before-and-after verification videos, and launching a rollout agent to monitor live production during deployment.

   "You can kind of think of it like hiring a high-powered lawyer who deals with you directly and owns strategy, but they farm out their tasks to a team of paralegals."

Teaching an AI to write a function is now table stakes, but teaching an autonomous colleague workplace judgment is still the Wild West. Today's frontier harnesses are busy making unmastered tasks feasible—guiding agents through complex web flows like building slide decks and booking travel, pacing communication so users stay informed without feeling overwhelmed, knowing when to ask permission before sending a risky email to a colleague, and learning a user's working style over time through memories.

3. Reason #2 the Broader Harness Is Vital: Infrastructure That Models Cannot Absorb

Skeptics of the harness often cite recent studies from UC Berkeley and Apple/EPFL, which tested frontier models across harnesses like Pi, Codex, and Claude Code and found that the choice of harness no longer made a significant difference in raw accuracy scores on SWE-bench Lite or machine learning engineering benchmarks.

   "A fancy harness in this day and age no longer adds coding intelligence."

While the internet fixated on flat evaluation scores, almost everyone overlooked a critical finding buried in both studies: the choice of harness created a massive difference in the cost per task. Furthermore, even the smartest model cannot natively absorb the runtime and operational layers outside its context window:

Cloud Runtime Persistence: Over the past year, typical agent tasks have expanded from minutes to hours, days, and longer. Because a personal laptop can go to sleep at any moment, Katz predicts that within six months, 90% of agent work will move off the laptop and into persistent cloud runtimes.

Enterprise Trust and Security: A bare-bones bash harness with all your API keys sitting in a text file might pass a coding eval, but in the real world, companies need permissions strictly scoped to specific agents and users—plus guardrails so no one wakes up to a catastrophic action or a $10,000 overnight API bill.

Cost and Speed Optimization: By tuning cache hit rates, token efficiency, and model mix inside the Grockbot harness, engineers significantly reduced costs and increased speed without any drop in quality—an advantage that compounds the more heavily you rely on agents. 

4. Modern Harnesses Use "Hyrum's Law" and Self-Deleting Code to Stay Clean

Because product innovation is once again moving faster than model releases, harnesses are entering a messy phase where engineers have to ship and unship features rapidly. Rather than waiting months for the next model checkpoint to fix a bad behavior—like when Grockbot takes too long to reply and needs a deterministic nudge saying a user is waiting—engineers deploy temporary hacks they call "shims".

To keep rapid iteration from turning the codebase into permanent spaghetti, the team relies on three disciplined engineering practices:

Applying Hyrum's Law: Because users eventually come to depend on any system detail exposed to them, modern harnesses intentionally hide more of their inner workings from the user, trading some visibility for much faster iteration and less change management.

Building Composable Primitives: Instead of building separate integrations every time an agent needs to wake up for a Slack post, a failing CI check on a pull request, or a scheduled time of day, the team built a single "subscriptions" primitive that lets agents subscribe to any event without requiring complex codebase refactors.

Automated "Shim" Cleanup: Every deterministic guardrail is tracked centrally and logged each time a model triggers it, allowing an automated bot to watch the dashboard and clean up obsolete hacks automatically.

   "Whenever a shim stops firing, that model or that agent will put up a PR and say this shim can be cleaned up."

Instead of letting legacy workarounds rot in production, the modern harness literally writes the pull request to delete its own training wheels the moment a new model outgrows them.

The Future Belongs to the Meta-Harness

"Yesterday's harness may be dead, but long live the agent harness of tomorrow."

The era of using wrapper code to make a model smarter at basic syntax is over. In its place is a far more ambitious architecture—one that orchestrates fleets of cloud agents, enforces enterprise security, optimizes token economics, and pioneers the next wave of autonomous knowledge work. As 90% of agent work prepares to leave our laptops for the cloud over the next six months, the real question for builders is no longer whether the agent harness will survive—it's what unmastered frontier your harness will teach the next generation of models to conquer next.

Key Takeaways

   - The Self-Obsoleting Flywheel: While the old coding-patch harness is fading because the data flywheel helped frontier models natively absorb basic coding skills, the broader agent harness is more vital than ever.

   - Unlocking New Frontiers: As basic coding is commoditized, modern harnesses step up to unlock unmastered domains like autonomous knowledge work in Grockbot and multi-agent "software factories".

   - Irreplaceable Infrastructure: Models cannot natively absorb non-context layers such as persistent cloud runtimes, scoped enterprise security permissions, and cost-per-task optimizations.

Baltimore just rejected a free offer to put its four Confederate monuments on public display—after keeping them mostly locked away in storage for nine years.

Emails obtained by The Baltimore Sun show the city turned down Confederate Memorial Park in St. Mary’s County. The park volunteered to exhibit the statues at no cost and even offered to include plaques written by Baltimore officials.

No explanation from the city. No permanent home. Just continued erasure of history that a city commission itself once called historical artifacts.

These monuments belong in public view so people can see them and decide for themselves. What should Baltimore do with them?
